#957. Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer

The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more?

Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers.

But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled.

While many expect that Balogun will get his move in January, to the Premier League or elsewhere, Monaco have understandably prepared for life without him. New manager Filipe Luís continues to prefer 20-year-old German youth international Paris Brunner to Balogun, giving the youngster ample time to tap into his vast potential. Balogun’s opportunities to turn the page have been limited.

On Sunday, though, Balogun took the first steps toward a brighter future, scoring the lone goal as Monaco fell 3-1 to Paris FC.

Monaco struggled to muster any meaningful chances in the first half against Paris, with Brunner sending the team’s only shot wide. Paris FC attacked relentlessly, stunning the early Ligue 1 title hopefuls with two goals just before half-time.

On days when Brunner puts it all together, such as when he bagged a brace against Marseille, he lives up to Luis’s faith. On other days, like Sunday, that faith can backfire. Enter Balogun.

Luís gave the American a chance to buck his months-long drought, bringing him on at half-time in place of Brunner, with a golden opportunity presenting itself in the 66th minute. Monaco broke up the right flank with a dribble from Brazilian right-back Vanderson, with Balogun running the channels while the Paris defense backtracked. Vanderson played a teasing low cross into the mixer that the goalkeeper couldn’t claim. Balogun needed just one prod, directing the ball to the far post. It wasn’t pretty, but it looked exceedingly comfortable, a rare return to the happy place that Balogun once frequented.

Just last season, Balogun finished fourth in Ligue 1’s goalscoring charts, bagging 13 for Monaco, with another six in the Champions League and the Coupe de France. His good form continued at the World Cup, with two first-half goals in the opening rout of Paraguay. His movement forced Australia into an own goal, with the Bosnia game providing him a third goal. Even in the expanded 48-team field in a particularly goal-saturated World Cup, only 10 players outscored him.

All of which only makes what came next even more complicated. Speaking with the media two days after the Bosnia game, Balogun called the entire red-card saga “surreal”, but refused to play victim. His message focused on making sure the next generation saw, through him, “the correct way to handle things, even when you think it’s unjust.” You really got the sense he wanted to move on from the whole episode.

Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.

Instead, Balogun has become an unwilling avatar in football fans’ suspicion of how football is run, one of the first names cited whenever Gianni Infantino is skewered for other controversial acts. He seems to have gotten grace for pulling the plug on joining David Moyes’s side, a sequence largely dismissed as “LOL Everton” fodder rather than an indictment of the player. But nonetheless, Balogun’s current standing at Monaco will hardly keep him operating at the requisite level to be a crucial player for Mauricio Pochettino. Luis also omitted Balogun from Monaco’s squad for the Uefa Conference League, limiting his participation to domestic competitions – where the manager has preferred Brunner.

A goal in a losing effort does not reverse any of this. But it may be the first step in Balogun’s quest to move past the events of the last few months – a timely reminder that with good service and a manager’s faith, he could still be a high-level scoring option. His time coming through Arsenal’s academy makes him a valuable prospect for Premier League suitors, nursing their homegrown player quotas for domestic and continental competition. Manchester United are reportedly one possibility, in case wants even more anxiety in his life; Juventus may be another.

More than goals, though, increased minutes would do wonders to help Balogun move on from a summer that’s redefined his reputation. While he still projects to be a rung above national team newcomers Julian Hall and Justin Ellis, the pair are starting games in MLS and scoring with regularity. It’s first-choice status that Balogun is yearning to hold once again.

#956. 'My job combines my passion for gaming and football'

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

We're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a new build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

So even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save."

So as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

So I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a new job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

One of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

To find out what other jobs you could have in football, explore the BBC Bitesize Follow Your Passion collection.

Ever wondered who makes sure your footy video games are great? This guy!

CJ works as an associate quality assurance manager on the video game Football Manager. His team test the game to make sure everything works, and collaborate with the developers to create the most realistic simulation of football.

There are lots of different ways to progress in the gaming industry.

CJ works in the QA (Quality Assurance) team, testing games. In this team, his career progression has followed this path:

His team is just one of the options, though. "There are lots of other roles within the industry too, including production, game design, social media and development, where developers help to code the game," he explains. "Depending on your skills and interests, there are different pathways you can take that you might enjoy and be suited to."

There are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the company you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

You could get into this role via a university course, a college course (such as a Level 3 Diploma in Creative Media, an A-level in Computing, or a T-level in Digital Software Development (England only)), an apprenticeship, or applying directly if you have relevant experience.

#955. Ever wondered what it's like to work on Match of the Day?

With its iconic theme tune, long established time in the weekend TV schedule, and expert analysis, Match of the Day is the most famous football show in the world. Each week the team at the BBC broadcast not one, but two, episodes â bringing viewers all the latest talking points from the Premier League.

Putting on this live broadcast is no easy task, thereâs so many different jobs that get the show to air. BBC Bitesize Careers went behind the scenes on a busy Sunday afternoon to meet just a small number of people involved and to find out more about how they got their jobs on the legendary show.

Cue the music. Do, do, do, dooo, do-do-do-do doooooooâ¦.

Joe Hart on why he loves his job on Match of the Day.

From production management assistants to make up artists, assistant producers to pundits, thereâs plenty of jobs that are involved in putting Match of the Day together each week. Isabelle Anastasiou on finding your next career step.

With a huge number of roles needed to get a live sports programme on to our screens itâs no surprise that the team at Match of the Day we spoke to all had different routes into the industry.

#954. From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini

Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter

Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas.

“I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!”

It took him another nine years to achieve that ambition. The Milan side he inherited in June did not look like the continental conquerors he used to admire on VHS. This version had just missed out on the Champions League for a second season running. Its hoped‑for star of this decade, Rafael Leão, was ready to move on amid laments of unfulfilled potential.

Still, from day one, Amorim has given off the air of a cat who got the cream. It was tempting to infer some relief at moving on from an unhappy chapter at Manchester United. Certainly it can’t have hurt that Milan’s owners backed their new manager to a tune of more than €160m (£132m) on transfer fees in the summer window.

But there was something in there too, of a person fulfilling a promise they made to their younger self. “Everybody knows Milan is one of my clubs since I was a boy,” Amorim said. “In my time as a young boy, Milan was the strongest team in Italy. And calcio was the best league in the world.”

Serie A lost that title some time ago. No Italian team have won the Champions League since 2010, and no player representing one has been awarded the Ballon d’Or since 2007. The Premier League long ago surpassed all rival competitions for TV revenues and spending power. Only a handful of super clubs elsewhere have kept up.

And yet, Serie A is having some kind of moment. Its reputation as the home of dour catenaccio is as outdated as Amorim’s old VCR, but things have spun especially far in the opposite direction this season, with an average of 3.18 goals per game. Italy’s top division has become home to some of the giddiest attacking football on the continent. Through almost 10 completed rounds there have been two 0-0 draws.

Bologna 2-1 Monza, Udinese 2-5 Roma, Milan 3-1 Inter, Como 1-0 Venezia, Frosinone 2-0 Torino, Lazio 2-1 Cagliari, Lecce 1-2 Genoa, Juventus 2-0 Napoli

Monday: Sassuolo v Fiorentina (5.30pm GMT), Atalanta v Parma (7.45pm GMT)

Amorim’s Milan have played their part. On Wednesday they endured their first league defeat, a barmy 4-2 loss at home against Bologna in which they fell behind early, came back to lead before half‑time then collapsed after the interval. Their manager cited exhaustion. An ominous thought, leading into the derby on Saturday. Inter had dropped only two points all season. Even their one draw felt more like a win, coming from two goals down to get a result away at Roma. Reigning champions, who reinforced the deepest squad in Serie A with the English trio of Curtis Jones, John Stones and Djed Spence in the summer, the Nerazzurri have been strong favourites to retain their title.

But after waiting a lifetime for a part in this fixture, Amorim was never going to arrive unprepared. If anything, the defeat by Bologna might have been influenced by his keeping one eye on the derby. Luka Modric and Christian Pulisic were left out of the starting XI in midweek, coming on only as second-half substitutes. Both lined up at kick-off against Inter. So did several other starters who had been deemed unfit even for a place on the bench against Bologna – Mario Gila, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira. Amorim sprung a surprise on top of that by naming the 20-year-old Sankhoun Diawara, whose only previous Milan start had been at centre-back, as his left wing-back in a 3-4-2-1.

The manager has shown more tactical flexibility at Milan than he did in Manchester, alternating his back three with a four. In the biggest game of his Milan tenure to date, however, Amorim returned to what he knows best. And Cristian Chivu copied him.

Inter’s manager was grappling with an availability crisis up front. Lautaro Martínez has been out for weeks with a hamstring strain, while Francesco Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny were unfit to start due to a virus. Chivu adapted by pushing Andy Diouf, a former midfielder who has been thriving at wing-back, forward to play on the right shoulder of Marcus Thuram, with Petar Sucic on the left.

But where the Nerazzurri looked unsure of themselves in a new system, Milan were straight into their stride. Pulisic put them in front in the fourth minute, his thumping header from Moreira’s cross the culmination of 80 seconds of unbroken possession. Rabiot then made it 2-0 in the 10th minute with a magnificent first-time flick across his body at a corner.

Inter’s defending, on both occasions, was horrendous, but that can be acknowledged without diminishing Milan’s design. The Rabiot goal was a rehearsed training ground routine, Diawara crossing paths with the Frenchman and blocking Hakan Calhanoglu’s attempts to track. Moreira was also flawless in his deliveries. The derby became his breakout moment, showing why Milan spent more than €50m to sign him from Strasbourg this summer.

Inter have recovered from losing positions five times already in this Serie A season, and three times from 2-0 down. They were threatening to repeat the trick after Alessandro Bastoni pulled a goal back from a corner. Spence forced a sensational save from Mike Maignan. But Milan won a free-kick, 20 yards out on the right. Moreira asked Modric to let him take it, then whipped a left‑footed shot over the wall into the near side of the net.

The game finished 3-1 to Milan, Inter’s first league defeat and a huge lift for Amorim. Despite being unbeaten themselves before the midweek defeat by Bologna, the Rossoneri have not always convinced. Even when controlling the tempo of games, they seem to lack clarity in the final third. Gonçalo Ramos, the club’s record signing, has not looked a natural fit as a lone striker, dropping deep too often when his team need a presence inside the box. He has scored just twice in 10 starts since his €73m move from Paris Saint-Germain.

Even this win raised questions. Can it really be the long-term vision for Moreira, the right wing‑back, to frequently hold a position on the pitch higher than the centre-forward?

Amorim was quick to insist on Saturday that no one should get carried away. He expressed delight for supporters and described the experience of his first Milan derby as unlike any other game of which he had been a part. But he also said Milan had been only good, not great, and noted that the three points here were only the same number they would have got by beating Bologna.

A sensible line to take. Milan have dominated this fixture lately – winning the past four derbies across all competitions and staying unbeaten in the past eight. Yet they have not finished above their neighbours since 2021-22, their last Scudetto-winning campaign.

Still, beating your greatest rival is always better than the alternative. The club’s owner, Gerry Cardinale, has been vocal in backing the new manager, telling La Gazzetta dello Sport last week that he was all in on “Amorim ball”. But in the week that Milan and Inter jointly presented plans for the new stadium that will replace San Siro in 2031, this result added weight to his assertion that the Rossoneri can contend for a Scudetto too.

#953. Why are some football shin pads so small?

Liverpool striker Lewis Koumas (second from left) sported low socks and small shinpads on his full Premier League debut at Anfield

Liverpool's Lewis Koumas made his full Premier League debut against Manchester City on Sunday.

While doing so, he sported some very low socks over what appeared to be a very small shin pad.

Last season, images of Burnley's Marcus Edwards went viral after the 27-year-old was seen wearing barely visible shin pads during a Premier League match against West Ham.

Two years ago, a picture of teenager Harry Howell celebrating with James Milner while they were Brighton team-mates also gained attention after fans noticed the visible difference in the size of their shin pads.

Howell's 'micro' pair were an obvious contrast to Milner's far more traditional-sized guards.

So what is behind the trend of extra-small shin guards, and why are they used instead of regular-sized pairs?

The simple answer is that players can choose what size shin pads they want to wear.

The International Football Association Board (Ifab), responsible for the laws of the game, say that shin pads are a mandatory piece of equipment players must wear while playing.

Be of an appropriate size to provide reasonable protection and be covered by the socks

And players are responsible for the size and suitability of their shin pads

The law does not define what an "appropriate" shin pad size is, but leave that decision to each individual player.

Shin pads provide vital protection for players to prevent serious injuries.

There has been a rising trend in younger footballers, as well as some big stars, wearing small shin pads during matches.

The reason for this could be for more comfort and to allow players to move around with greater ease.

Referees are only required to check that some form of shin guards are being worn, Ifab told BBC Sport.

Ifab said players - or the parents or guardians of youth players - must take responsibility for their own safety on the pitch.

While shin pad size is ultimately an individuals choice, any decisions around player safety would also be made in consultation with their club and medical staff.

Marcus Edwards last year was seen wearing very small shin pads for Burnley in the Premier League

Grassroots football teams have started to ban small shin pads for safety reasons.

There are concerns that small shin pads do not cover the shins properly, which can lead to an increased risk of injury - especially at non-elite level.

In August 2024, a football club banned small shin pads after a youth player suffered a double leg break.

Penistone Church player Alfie Collins broke his tibia and fibula in a tackle during a game. The teenager's shin pads, which were no bigger than a credit card, were similar to a size recently worn by some stars of the professional game.

Shin pads "play an important role in injury prevention as they are intended to protect the shin from injury", the Football Association said.

"'Micro' or 'mini' shin pads may therefore increase the risk of injury due to the smaller amount of shin covered compared to larger sized shin pads," they added.

#952. Love Is Blind Star Michaella Giorgio’s Romance With Costar Revealed

Love is Blind’s season 11 reunion revealed that Michaella Giorgio and beekeeper Matt Waldrip tested their connection out in the real world following her breakup with Rob Feeley.

After trying her hand at love sight unseen, Michaella Giorgio went into a second romance with eyes wide open.

During the Love Is Blind season 11 reunion on Nov. 8, it was revealed that after she and Rob Feeley ended their engagement, Michaella and her other in-pod connection Matt Waldrip (known as “the beekeeper”) gave their chemistry a try.

The news was revealed by Matt after host Nick Lachey asked if he ever, or still did, have feelings for Michaella.

“Man, where to start on that?” he said. “I'll just come out and say, Michaella and I did have a relationship after the experiment ended. You know, I feel genuinely lucky that such a remarkable woman found it worth her while to welcome me into her life after all of this and meet her family. You met my family.”

He added, “Ultimately, I did fall in love with you during that time, and I'm sorry that I'm the one that ended it. I genuinely wish you all the happiness and success in the world, Michaella. You're a queen, you're always going to hold a special place in my heart, for sure. And if you ever need anything—”

A heated Michaella, however, stopped the beekeeper mid-thought.

“I need nothing,” she said. “I need nothing. I need nothing. Newsflash, nothing.”

She also shared her take on what went down between them—and it may not have been all that sweet.

“Matt and I had a really great friendship that shouldn't have crossed friendship,” she said. "I think that's definitely an exaggeration of our relationship. We dated for a few weeks, and I dropped you off at your mom's house and met your mother. I don't think we were in love.”

Matt, however, said he had been in love with her, and that Michaella had accompanied the single father to Harry Potter and the Cursed Child with his family, also noting Michaella’s mother makes “mean chicken cutlets.”

“It was very meaningful to me,” he added, “so I'm sorry that you don't remember it the same way.”

Michaella then noted, “I did say I love you, but I did not say I was in love with you. We're going to be transparent: I was on mushrooms, which you knew that I took.”

Matt called her recollection of events “just a shame,” adding he was glad he didn’t bring the homemade honey he’d thought about gifting her to the reunion.

As for the connection that first ended in an engagement, but then a broken heart, Michaella shared some final words for Rob during the reunion.

“I have no regrets. I really fell in love with you,” she said. “I will love you forever, you know, and it's a shame how things turned out, but we're all good.”

Meanwhile, Rob shared his well wishes for his former fiancée.

“Everything that I said was genuine from the day I met you to even today, just looking at you, like it brings back so many memories,” he said. “And I let you down, so, I apologize for that. You deserve better, and you're definitely gonna find something better.”

He concluded, “And if you need me for anything, you can text me, call. Like you have a friend in me.”

For more on where the couples on Love is Blind stand today, read on.

Though yacht captain Blake’s romance with marketing manager Erika appeared to be smooth sailing after the pods, just one week before their wedding, the couple realized they may be in too deep due to their dramatically different lifestyles.

“I don’t want to hold you back,” Blake told Erika during the season 11 finale. “I don’t want you to be that captain’s wife on the widow walk. I don’t want to marry you and then for you to feel held hostage while I’m sailing around, gone for weeks on end. And then you’ve got a timeline with kids and everything.”

“I just think at this point, there’s too many concerns, too many questions that I can’t say yes at the altar,” she shared. “I just think the best thing to do is to leave the experiment.”

And while Erika cried over their decision, Blake had already concluded their ship had sailed.

“The experiment is done, but it’s the right move,” Blake confirmed. And when a producer asked if he ever had a love like this, he replied: “I’m not gonna answer that one…I’m feeling a little relieved, a little exhausted.”

While both Wilson and Wilnie had the times of their lives at their respective bachelor and bachelorette celebrations, the party was definitely over before they reached the altar.

In fact, they couldn’t see eye-to-eye on life's more mundane tasks, including dividing up cooking duties and household chores.

“When we got out of the pods, you got everything I promised you, plus,” Wilson told Wilnie following an off-camera disagreement, later adding, “You said it countless times, ‘I’ll do the things for you that make you happy.’ And I’ve mentioned what those things might be, but then you’ll be like, ‘But I don’t like doing that…I’m not used to doing that.’”

As for Wilnie, she couldn’t disagree more. “I don’t work in the home,” the mental health counselor explained. “I have long, emotionally draining days and whether you agree with that, when I get home, it is hard for me to always be at your level.”

Ultimately, for Wilson, there were too many issues at hand for them to tie the knot. “It’s not that you’re a bad person,” the senior compliance manager shared, “you’re a phenomenal person but maybe marriage is not for us.”

By the end, though a tearful Wilnie confirmed she still loved Wilson, she doesn’t regret their path.

Once Aneha and Cam entered the real world, her hesitation to marry someone with a different background and religious beliefs —especially in the wake of her family’s disapproval—and their communication skills proved to be hurdles. And, yet, they seemed determined to scale them together.

However, once asked whether she was ready to say “I do,” the principal engineer shared that she couldn’t, telling her fiancé: “I still believe you’re my person, but I do not today. I need more time.”

As for Cam, he assured her that he completely understood. “It’s okay,” the human resource coordinator replied. “it’s a big decision. I feel like we both need to be one hundred percent confident.”

But once Aneha declared she didn’t and danced away from the altar while stressing to Cam that he was still her fiancé, he teared up watching her leave. As he later explained to his family, he simply didn’t “know what happens now.”

Shortly after, Aneha and Cam did end up meeting up one final time. And while Cam expressed that he still loved and cared for her, he needed time to process the “I don’t” of it all.

The result of that processing was revealed at the reunion on Nov. 8, 2026, when the pair confirmed they had parted ways for good shortly after saying no at the altar.

When healthcare worker Sarah started to fall for account executive John, they initially disagreed on fundamental topics such as abortion rights and vaccinations. However, despite their perspectives, they both said yes to spending their lives together, becoming the only couple to get married during the show’s 11th season.

“It’s fun looking back on the first few days ‘cause I don’t think we liked each other very much,” she shared. “And then, some people here heard the story about you maybe not being too jazzed to keep talking to me. But I love that that happened, because I think that was a catalyst for us.”

She noted, “After that, I’ve never been so sure on someone, and I had never even seen you. And then when I saw you, I felt like I’d already known you a lifetime.”

Just before the season's reunion aired, however, court documents showed Sarah filed for divorce just over a year after they tied the knot. And at the reunion, John revealed he had exchanged inappropriate texts with a stripper and escort he'd met during a boys' night out.

For Sarah, it marked the final push she needed to leave their marriage after a year, during which time she said John could be hurtful in the way he communicated to her.

Even though the pair were shaping up to be frontrunners once they left the pods, Rob and Michaella’s relationship came to a screeching halt after he had two shocking public outbursts during episode 10.

After a hangout with his fellow friends went left once a bartender cut one of them off, Rob then came to the cast meet-up with another bone to pick.

"I’m going down in this thing as the biggest piece of s--t,” he yelled at the bar. “Right where Netflix wants me, buddy. Dude, they’re gonna manipulate this whole thing into something crazy. I don’t give a f--k."

In fact, his behavior amongst his castmates—in addition to other uncomfortable moments between the two of them—made Michaella think twice about completing the rest of their journey.

"I don’t deserve any of what I’m getting," she expressed through tears. "I love him. It’s just a lot. And we’re not getting married. I cannot marry this man under any circumstances."

Scott “Stew” Stewart & Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli: Split—But Friendly

Despite their initial chemistry in the pods, Stew and Jax fizzled out almost immediately once they met face-to-face.

However, even after ending their engagement, they’ve coming to a crystal-clear understanding as friends. In fact, Stew shared that even though Jax had turned down producers’ offer to meet up again immediately after their reveal, she then reached out on her own terms.

"It was super sincere," he previously told E! News. "She explained that it wasn't about me. It was about just the emotional overload of the previous couple weeks, and I think once we got settled back in Boston, once kind of normal life was allowed to resume, we were able to kind of catch our breaths."

At the reunion, Stew and Jax confirmed they've stayed in touch and even live near each other in Boston. While neither was ready to ask the other out on air, their attitude was very much "never say never" about their future. Jax did confirm she turned her engagement ring into a pinky ring which she wears everyday.

Heading into their big day, Amber—who is mom to daughter Emma—expressed worry over Jordan actually saying “I do” when it came time.

But, her fears were put to rest as the two both ended up saying yes, leaving almost everyone present to shed tears, including her daughter.

However, their relationship came to an end just four months later, the former couple revealed during an emotional face-off at the March 2026 season 10 reunion.

Brittany Wicker & Devonta Anderson: Split

Right before their nuptials, season 10's Brittany revealed she was “shocked” when Devonta called it all off.

“Today was supposed to be our wedding day but it’s not,” she told the camera. “But right now, I feel like everything I want isn’t happening.”

As for her now ex, though Devonta noted that everything between then was “great,” ultimately, “I can’t walk into a marriage with self-doubt of ‘Can I love you how you need to be loved?’ I think that’s why I couldn’t get to the altar. I just can’t do it.”

And though Brittany walked away noting that they’re “still going to be together,” Devonta confirmed he’s not on the same page.

Indeed, Devonta revealed at the March 2026 reunion that he is now engaged to an old friend and the two are expecting a baby. The pair welcomed son Kyler Lee Anderson in August 2026.

Brianna “Breezy” McNees & Connor Spies: Split

Though season 10 star Bri decided she and Connor weren’t ready to get married just days before their wedding, at the show’s March 2026 reunion, the pair confirmed they’re still very much in love and working on eventually getting to their happily ever after.

But their journey reached a hard stop weeks later, Connor sharing on the Table for 1 podcast in June, "I'm not dating Bri anymore."

The season 10 couple's engagement came to an abrupt end once Chris confessed to Jessica that he wasn't physically attracted to her.

However, Jessica has since found love in another pod mate, as she revealed at the March 2026 reunion, with fellow doctor Haramol Gill.

"You are everything, Jess," Haramol told her during the special. "Every room you walk into gets brighter."

Though the season 10 pair nearly exchanged vows after falling in love sight unseen, their differing perspectives on having kids—Emma has voiced her uncertainty while Mike has been firm about having them—was too much of a factor to compromise on.

“I do love you,” Mike told Emma. “Right now, I’m not ready to say I do. I want kids. And I want to know that you definitely, 100 percent want a family with me. I don’t wanna say yes and jump into something and then it changes down the road.”

And though Emma noted she can “see glimpses of a family,” in their future, Mike shared that he wants to her to be certain.

"If we’re gonna get married, I want you to know that you want a family with me for sure,” he explained. “I don’t want it to be half-ass…And you have your reasons and I respect them and respect them but I just can’t say yes without knowing that. So, I’m sorry."

Mike has since hard-launched a new romance.

Before walking down the aisle in the season 10 finale, the soccer coach compared his wedding day to a “penalty shootout with everything on the line,” noting that he was confident that they would make it.

However, Ashley made it clear that it wouldn’t be the goal and jumped in when he was presented with whether he would say “I do.”

"I know what you’re going to say," she told him. "I know you don’t choose me and I’m not choosing you either.” Ashley went on to list a number of reasons why they didn’t work out, including questions about his integrity. A point Alex made sure to address in that very same moment.

"I do disagree to an extent about the integrity," he told her. "I felt as though the questions about my past were more to try and catch me in something than really understand me."

And if you’re wondering whether he would do anything differently: "Absolutely no regrets on my end, I’m so pleased and proud of myself as a person."

Victor "Vic" St. John & Christine Hamilton: Married

From the start of season 10, Christine and Vic were instantly a match made in pod heaven, with the two both happily agreeing to their future together.

"I never thought I would fall in love in such a unique experiment, and Christine,” he noted during his vows, “the moment we spoke in those pods, we just connected…You know more about me than anyone else on this planet."

She marked his 35th birthday in September with an Instagram tribute to "the kindest, most hardworking, humble, strong, gentle, passionate, joyful, God-fearing man."

In the end, Anton's drinking habits and financial situation didn't seem to match what Ali was seeking.

"I can't be your wife," she told the truck driver at the altar in season nine. "The person I fell in love with in the pods isn't the person I've gotten to experience in real life."

"It just didn't feel right or how I would expect that moment to feel like," she told the cameras. "I don't feel he was super forthcoming about his lifestyle."

Anton's reaction? "I don't know if it's looks, I don't know if it's the vibes or I don't know if it's the way that we were living together. But I can say I've done nothing but care for her."

Though the couple bonded over having loved ones with Type 1 diabetes, their differing lifestyles (he preferred a more simplistic way of life; she loves luxury) were a breaking point for Megan, who called off the wedding at the end of the season nine finale.

"We're ships in the night, like two different people," the entrepreneur told him. But the metaphor passed him by, with Jordan insisting, "I don't see it."

When Megan cited his picky eating habits and his inflexible travel schedule as a dad, Jordan told her, "I don't know why you chose me in the pods then."

"Initially I leaned into opposites attract but I still just have reservations," she explained before they each began crying. "Knowing this today, there's no way I wanted to go to the altar and put either of us through that."

Jordan shared his one regret was introducing her to his son, Luca, saying in a confessional, "I feel like she doesn't love me for me and that's the closure I need."

Megan admitted the ordeal had her "questioning if I'm even cut out to be a mom. Maybe I am too caught up in my own life."

But at the October 2025 reunion, she revealed she and partner Paul Wegman had welcomed a son they named Brooks.

Kalybriah Haskin & Edmond L. Harvey: Split

They both confessed they "love the hell out of" each other at the altar, but season nine's Kalybriah turned Edmond down with an apology.

"You deserve someone that is 100 percent at the altar and I'm not 100 percent right now," she told the realtor. Still, she stressed, "My no doesn't mean that I don't love you."

While Edmond broke down in tears, Kalybriah thanked him for being "so graceful" as she made the "hard" decision. When he asked if she'd date him "down the road," Kalybriah said she'd never write him off.

"I am shocked," he said in a confessional of her decision. "There was no bright side."

The pair didn't make it to the altar in season nine, as Joe ended the relationship after having a breakdown at his tux fitting.

"On and off camera, Joe was different," Madison later told Glamour. "Off camera, he was far more reassuring. We were very intimate, very touchy. And then on camera, it was the opposite, and you kind of see that at the pool party."

Madison even asked Joe about his attraction for her, which he confessed was an issue during their vacation.

"I kind of dug deeper, like, 'What is your typical type?' And he was like, 'I just usually date more petite women,'" she recalled to the outlet. "I am a really confident person. At that moment, it kind of put me into this insecure feeling."

Joe defended his comment, telling the outlet, “I was trying, poorly, to explain a pattern in my past dating experiences, not to compare or criticize."

Nick dumped Annie before the wedding day in season nine, explaining he was hurt that she continued to say she loved him more than he loved her.

However, the hairstylist refused to believe it was over and tried to convince Nick to continue, saying, "Just be in this and love me."

"You can't make one plus one equal three," he said, prompting her to say, "Watch me."

Nick ultimately told Annie, “The reason that I am not willing to marry you is because I am unhappy."

Lauren O'Brien and David Bettenburg: Split

Their romance failed to take off once the season eight pair landed in Honduras, with Dave revealing he and his then-fiancée had mutual friends in common. But it wasn’t the similar inner circles that proved to be the problem, but rather, Dave’s hesitation in moving forward after they told him about Lauren hooking up with someone they knew before the show.

Not to mention, Dave also didn’t want to introduce Lauren to his friends and family, noting that his dad didn’t know of his engagement and that his sister—who became a big point of contention—disapproved of their relationship altogether.

One of the most compatible couples of season eight, most viewers assumed Monica and Joey would make it down the aisle and beyond. However, when it came to saying "I do," Monica instead said, "I don’t right now."

"In this moment, it's 100 percent," she said through tears, "and I just feel like we're both, we're not quite there." As for Joey, he agreed with every word.

“That's totally okay,” he explained after hugging her. “I think we both have a tremendous amount of love for each other, and that's apparent. But I think there's bigger things and bigger growth. And I agree, I don’t think I would be ready. And to be completely honest, I’m also not 100 percent at this time.”

Though season eight's Ben and Sara seemed to disagree on major components of their life together—including religion and politics—by wedding day, the pair seemed to have gotten on the same page. But ultimately, they decided to end their shared story.

As Sara—who said, "I don’t" to a future with Ben—explained, "Ben, I love you so much but I always wanted a partner to be on the same wavelength, and so today, I can't. I'm sorry but I don't want that to be misunderstood."

She later added, "I know that the connection we have is so real and my heart is there, but when we talked about a lot of the values I hold so close to my heart, making this decision, my mind is telling me I can't."

Another season eight couple who seemed to be focused on the road ahead post-pods, Devin and Virginia, got along perfectly fine—that is, until the topic of having a prenup came up.

But it was even bigger issues that proved to be enough for Virginia, leading her to ultimately saying no to spending the rest of her life with Devin.

“I think that in a lot of our relationship, I wanted to protect Devin,” she said, through tears, after the leaving the altar. “And I don't know if that's a cultural thing, but it's always been important for me to protect him. So, there were even topics that he didn't want to talk about, like politics, there were just certain things he just didn't want me to push on. So there was just depths of our relationship that we didn't get to. We just didn't get there.”

There was at least one season eight couple who did say yes to a season of love past Christmas.

Though the pair seemed to face quite the hurdle (Taylor was convinced Daniel followed, then unfollowed her on Instagram before the show and therefore, knew what she looked like), they managed to clear that particular obstacle.

In fact, after exchanging emotional vows, the two enjoyed a beautiful wedding and celebratory reception.

"We did it," Daniel said while sitting alongisde Taylor after their nuptials, with Taylor adding, "We're so excited to start the next chapter." They marked two years of their "wild journey" with a March 2026 Instagram post.

Brittany Wisniewski and Leo Braudy: Split

Though the now-famed art dealer decided to pop the question to the Keeping Well author following his season seven love triangle with Hannah Jiles, the pair ultimately decided after their short engagement, they were better off as friends.

“The chemistry just wasn't there,” Brittany previously told People in a joint interview with Leo. “We had a talk in the beginning about how this could work and then time went on during the trip and the chemistry just wasn't there and we mutually felt that. We're very good communicators, so it was not a big ordeal. It was a very clean, respectful realization.”

Shortly after her appearance on the Netflix dating show, Brittany debuted her romance with musician Mod Sun in November 2024, but she confirmed in July 2025 that the pair had called it quits.

Monica Davis and Stephen Richardson: Split

Monica and Stephen’s relationship came to a screeching halt in season seven when she uncovered “really kinky” sext messages sent between her fiancé and another woman, causing the pair to break up shortly after they arrived home from Mexico. As for Stephen, he apologized in the moment during episode eight, but he also shared a message on social media once the episode aired.

"I hope I didn't ruin anyone's day by existing," he wrote on Instagram Stories in October 2024, "and if I did, I'm sorry you had to wake up this morning. I wish you didn't have to either. But I'll love you all the same."

Once Hannah and Nick embarked on life outside the pods, the season seven pair had their fair share of ups and downs—and disagreements—to say the least. (Let’s not forget: “I think you get treated as an equal when you star contributing like an equal.”)

And it all came to a head when Hannah decided they wouldn’t make it down the aisle. As for Nick, he called their breakup “one of the worst feelings of my life.”

Since then, Hannah has admitted the show forced her to do some self-introspection.

“I’ve learned a lot, I’ve learned there’s things I need to work on,” she said during an October 2024 episode of The Viall Files podcast. “For example, I am a very direct person. I know that but I think my delivery is rough. And I’ve learned that delivery is everything.”

Taylor Krause and Garrett Josemans: Married

A match made in science-based heaven (i.e. those serendipitous tattoos), season seven stars Taylor and Garrett clicked from the very beginning and just seemed destined to say, “I do.” Though they did hit a rough patch once Taylor found out he responded to an ex’s DM (according to Garrett, he confirmed he was engaged and shut it down), the rest is Love Is Blind history.

"I'm very grateful to have a life partner like my husband because no matter where we are in the world you make it feel like home," Taylor wrote in a November 2025 Instagram post marking their second anniversary. "I admire how much we have grown to build a life together and much of that has been because of you."

Yes, you read that right: Though Marissa and Ramses rose to become one of season seven's frontrunners of the couples who would make it, he ultimately called off their wedding after having second thoughts.

“We have a great future ahead of us, I want to marry you,” Marissa told her fiancé after a sit-down to which he responds, “I understand falling in love is a risk, I understand that.”

However, he noted their differences—which have included his stance on the military—may be too tough to work through. “After being married and seeing other marriages and hearing from other married people,” he added. “I just don’t think love alone is enough…I think there needs to be other things that are also working.”

As for Marissa, though she tried to navigate past their perspectives, once she confirmed it was over, she broke down into tears. “I don’t think you should’ve come to this experience,” she tells him. “How could I feel so sure? And you’re not? It sucks, I want you to choose me,” adding of their split, “This is the worst day of my life.”

She announced her marriage to former partner D. Johnson in May 2026.

Tyler Francis and Ashley Adionser: Divorced

Tyler and Ashley quickly became a fan-favorite couple after season seven viewers watched their relatively easy-going romance unfold. However, the couple hit a bump in the road once Tyler shared that he had three children, which Ashley referred to as his "sperm donor babies." (However, there’s online discourse over the extent of his involvement, which he has not addressed publicly).

By the October 2024 reunion episode, Ashley and Tyler were able to move past this fact and went on to not only reconnect—but in fact, become husband and wife.

“We started this journey two months ago and this changed our entire lives,” Tyler says while sitting alongside Ashley after their wedding. “Now, we get to spend the rest of our lives together.”

However, Ashley later shared that the pair had called it quits following over one year of marriage.

"After much reflection, I want to share that Tyler and I have been separated for several weeks and have now made the difficult decision to end our marriage," she told People in a January 2025 statement. "While I had hoped for mutual understanding and transparency in our relationship, it has become clear that our paths are no longer aligned, making it impossible for me to continue in this marriage."

Season seven stars Alex and Tim seemed to smooth over their major disagreement in Mexico by the time they got back home to Washington, D.C. In fact, Tim had an emotional meeting with Alex’s dad that seemed to cement their future.

However, after Alex met with Tim’s family, they got into yet another argument and Tim ended their engagement by telling Alex that he didn’t ever want to see her again. Since then, both have spoken out to defend themselves after the breakup, with Alex noting that their split was not “a mutual decision.”

#951. Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

#950. Who is close to a yellow card suspension in Champions League?

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

Shakhtar Donetsk's Marlon Gomes, Villarreal's Santiago Mourino and Inter Milan's Hakan Calhanoglu are each on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

*denotes two yellows that resulted in a red card

The following players will miss the next round of league phase matches following either a yellow or red card suspension:

Matheus Cunha (Manchester United - red card suspension)

#949. Amanda Seyfried Reveals Her Daughter's Reaction to Mean Girls

Amanda Seyfried shared her daughter Nina's reaction to watching Mean Girls for the first time during an exclusive E! News interview at the Steps world premiere in NYC.

Amanda Seyfried's fifth sense is knowing when to show her kids her work.

Although the Mean Girls alum and ex Thomas Sadoski's kids Nina, 9, and Thomas Jr., 6, aren't fully versed in her filmography, when it comes to what they have seen, they think she's pretty grool.

"They've seen the few animated movies I've done," Seyfried exclusively told E! News at the world premiere of her new Netflix movie Steps on Nov. 8. "My daughter watched Mean Girls for the first time last year. They love it."

Her kids know that she's not a regular mom, she's a cool mom.

"It's normal for them," the 40-year-old said of her career being in the spotlight. "I'm learning more every day. I think as they get older, they're like, 'Huh, what a very unique place to get to be.' I'm like, 'Yeah, it is unique!'"

And when it comes to expressing gratitude, for Seyfried, the limit does not exist.

Along with pressing play on the Lindsay Lohan-led movie—also starring Rachel McAdams, Tina Fey and Jonathan Bennett—her kids have also taken a chance on some of her other biggest hits.

The Dropout star—who announced her breakup from Sadoski in September after nine years of marriage—added, "They loved Mamma Mia."

Now, Nina and Thomas Jr. are watching the Oscar nominee find her happily ever after in Steps—premiering on Netflix Nov. 20—as Cinderella.

Although the animated movie is a reimagining of the fairy tale—in which the princess' stepsisters Lilith (Ali Wong) and Margot (Stephanie Hsu) are misunderstood, rather than evil, as they team up to save the kingdom from childhood bully Priscilla (Nikki Glaser)—it simply expands on the already beloved story.

"I saw her as somebody who was desperately searching for herself in some way," Seyfried said. "That hasn't changed. But I think we've really gone into this book, this fairy tale, this story that we all know, and they've completely upended it."

"It took the complexity of who we are as people in the world and turned it into this unique depiction of sisterhood and friendship," she continued, "and what it takes to fully be able to communicate and bond."

Seyfried will definitely be adding Steps to her kids' movie night queue. "It's beautiful," she beamed. "This is what I want my kids to be watching."

#948. Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

Palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

The England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

In most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

#947. Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban

The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 13 players sitting on four bookings after 10 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have served a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards)

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four)

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:

Max Dowman - Arsenal (red card suspension)

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension)

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension)

#946. Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell

Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table

It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy.

In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister.

Dortmund, however, did not read the script. Neither did the football gods. Kane was not completely neutered in this and laid on yet another assist, nodding across goal to present Dayot Upamecano a second goal in successive Bundesliga games That looked like the winner until Fábio Silva’s 89th-minute equaliser for the visitors. Yet in between, there was frustration for the man who has walked on water since arriving in Munich. He clattered a penalty which could have made it 2-0 against the crossbar and hit the post from point-blank range when he could have made it 3-1, after Serhou Guirassy’s first equaliser and the Upamecano strike that put Bayern back in front.

Three years ago on Wednesday, Kane hit a hat-trick in his first Klassiker in a 4-0 win at Signal Iduna Park. Despite the cliche that BVB are Bayern’s bunnies, the champions have not had it all their own way in this fixture. This was Kane’s fourth Klassiker at the Allianz Arena, and Bayern have only won one of them. Many of those watching from around the world who tuned in to see Kane lift his personal trophy would have expected a subsequent procession to victory but having arrived level on points at the top of the table, Dortmund were able to leave Bavaria in the same position.

This was, as Ruhr Nachrichten’s Kevin Pinnow put it, “much more than just a point” for Dortmund. It was not a signal they are Bayern’s equal but a sign they could roll with the punches, that they could show guts and enterprise and find solutions, from the switch to a back four that blind-sided their hosts to the energy and daring in midfield, exemplified by Jobe Bellingham’s best performance since he arrived last year. The young Englishman is a symbol of the good Niko Kovac has done since arriving at the club, a combination of patience and high demand. The coach insisted earlier this year that Bellingham, despite a lack of numerical reward, was progressing ahead of schedule and this, finally was the proof. He might even have put BVB in front in the first half, but had a goal ruled out as the offside Carney Chukwuemeka – who also excelled – inadvertently stumbled into Jonas Urbig in the Bayern goal. “He is someone for the big stake,” enthused the sporting director, Ole Book. “He showed that today.”

SV Elversberg 4-1 Mainz, Augsburg 1-2 Freiburg, Mönchengladbach 0-0 Paderborn, Schalke 0-2 RB Leipzig, Werder 2-0 Hoffenheim, Leverkusen 2-4 VfB Stuttgart, Bayern 2-2 Dortmund, Union Berlin 1-1 Köln, Eintracht Frankfurt 3-1 Hamburg

Yet as worthy as Dortmund were, little went for Bayern. The bad luck was not limited to plural pinging of aluminium and the effects will last for longer than Monday morning. Already without Vincent Kompany, who will not be rushed back into action after his recent hospitalisation with his assistant, Aaron Danks, holding the fort, the injury list is getting out of hand. Danks went into this fixture without Luis Díaz, Manuel Neuer and Jamal Musiala and lost a further three forward players during the course of the evening.

Ismael Saibari injured his ankle ligaments in a collision with Gregor Kobel and has already had surgery, with the recovery to last at least three months. Serge Gnabry is expected to miss several weeks with a hamstring injury he picked up and, worst of all, Michael Olise went down off the ball with what appeared to be a knee problem in the closing minutes. Bayern will go into this week’s Champions League game with Atlético Madrid – surely the last game they would wish to face with a banged-up squad – with only two senior forward players available, Kane and the 18-year-old Lennart Karl.

Karl still almost won the game for the hosts, bending a shot from range against the top of the crossbar in stoppage time He might have many other chances to make himself the hero in the games to come. As will Kane, again and again. We will see quite how the immediate post-Ballon d’Or period will unfold. One of Kane’s key characteristics throughout his career has been his relentless availability, but part of his ascension to his best-ever self has been based on Kompany’s ability to rest his star turn and keep him fresh. With the current plethora of injuries, Danks is unlikely to have the same luxury.

It is impossible to talk about turning points in the season on Halloween. Yet Kane will be loading Bayern on his broad shoulders ever more than before, and Dortmund’s next challenge is to be brave enough to try to take advantage.

If Sebastian Hoeness and his Stuttgart team were going to lift themselves out of a crisis of confidence it was always going to be not by eking out a gritty result, but by blasting their way back to health, and that is what they did at Leverkusen, winning 4-2 in a fixture that has been one of the Bundesliga’s must-watch match-ups of recent seasons. For all their attacking punch, Hoeness and company arrived having lost four out of five on the back of some profligate finishing. Here they were clinical in a testy game against a Werkself team who had chances of their own. “Unfortunately, we can’t play Leverkusen 34 times,” lamented the Champions League joint top scorer Ermedin Demirovic, who scored twice. “They’re always heated and exciting matches because both teams play with attacking intent.”

Leipzig strolled to a 2-0 win at an impotent Schalke – still yet to score a home goal – before facing Manchester City, an important step to Martín Demichelis shoring up his position. The Norwegian winger Antonio Nusa, who scored one and made one, excelled.

Niclas Füllkrug was at it again for Werder Bremen, after an attempted midweek DFB Pokal rescue act at his old club Borussia Dortmund, scoring twice to bring Werder level before their hopes were dashed by a late Marcel Sabitzer winner. The centre-forward blasted the northerners into the lead on Saturday against Hoffenheim, setting up a win that pushes them into the top five. It was his seventh straight Bundesliga game scoring, equalling the legendary Rudi Völler’s record from 1982-83. “I’m truly speechless,” said the goalkeeper Karl Hein, whose huge clearance set the goal up. “It’s a privilege to have him with us.” Even with his plan to revitalise Germany and make the squad younger, it is hard to see how Jürgen Klopp can omit Füllkrug when he announces his next Germany squad on Thursday.

#945. England Wheelchair rout Australia to reach World Cup final

England Wheelchair beat Australia 86-18 to reach fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final; Rob Hawkins led the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance; England face France in World Cup final in Wollongong on Friday

England Wheelchair scored a record points total against rival Australia to rout their opponents 86-18 and reach their fifth successive Rugby League World Cup final.

The game was all but over at half-time as England held a 40-6 lead, with Rob Hawkins leading the charge for his side with a stunning 30-point performance in his side's dominant victory.

The win means the defending World Cup champions will face France in the final in Wollongong on Friday, with a chance to claim their third World Cup title.

Mason Billington - who picked up Player of the Match - opened the scoring in just the third minute of the contest with a try, before Hawkins added two of his own and back Joe Coyd got in on the act to put England in firm control with a 30-0 lead after just 24 minutes.

Diab Karim eventually got the host nation on the scoresheet with a converted try, but their joy was short-lived after Billington went over twice to seal his hat-trick before half-time.

Interchanges Jack Brown and Nathan Collins scored three tries between them in the opening 10 minutes of the second half before Hawkins struck twice more to put England out of reach.

Karim and Dan Antsey went over for consolations just after the hour mark, but tries from Chris Haynes and the captain Lewis King put the finishing touches on a sensational victory for the two-time World Champions.

England Wheelchair rugby league captain Lewis King:

I don't want to put a number on it but we are proud of that performance, we were super disciplined in how we wanted to play. We had a game plan and we executed it. I am super proud."

"I am grateful for the opportunity [to be captain] and I don't want to take putting this badge on as an opportunity because you don't know how many times you will get to do it.

"I am excited for the opportunity. The culture of this team is teammates we are like brothers. I am looking forward to Friday.

"When we meet France, it is always down to the finer details and margins, so I won't be thinking about France, we will be focused on us."

#943. American Idol's Justin Guarini Details "Dark Place" After Career Stall

Justin Guarini—runner-up to Kelly Clarkson on the debut season of American Idol in 2002—shared that he struggled with his mental health when his career took an unexpected pause.

Justin Guarini is shining a spotlight on one of his darkest chapters.

In his new book Center Stage Confidence, the American Idol alum—who came in as Kelly Clarkson’s runner-up on the singing competition show’s debut season in 2002—shared insight into the lowest moment of his career, saying his success plummeted after he was dropped by his record label RCA in 2003.

“I stared at the TV in shock as my entire world came crumbling down around my ears,” Guarini, who said he learned the news during a Weekend Update segment on Saturday Night Live, wrote in his book, per Fox News Digital. “Every illusion of fame, fortune, and glory fell away in an instant—only to be replaced by the silence of loss.”

He continued, “In that moment, the veil of my arrogance, my assumptions, and my entitlement were lifted away, and I saw my life for what it had become.”

Following his run on American Idol, Guarini released his self-titled debut album in 2003, which landed in the top 20 of the Billboard 200 charts, and starred in a romantic comedy with Clarkson called From Justin to Kelly.

But neither project wound up catapulting his career as he’d hoped.

“I spent months playing my sad story on repeat,” he wrote. “I lost weight, slept more and more, and became less and less like myself, and the people who loved me started to notice and worry. I was living the ghost of the life I had always dreamed of and burning money and time in equal and absurd measure.”

Indeed, as his career stalled, Guarini—dad to two sons with ex Reina Capodici—struggled to reconcile with the cards he’d been dealt.

“There have been plenty of people who’ve given up and failed and found other things,” Guarini told Fox News Digital in an interview published Nov. 8. “That’s really wonderful. But for me, that dark place of not wanting to get out of bed, not wanting to look at myself in the mirror, not wanting to go out and see anything, it just was a period of isolation. And it’s very easy to do when you live behind a gate in an exclusive community.”

But now, the 48-year-old sees the lull in his career as a blessing in disguise.

“I think it was one of the greatest things that could ever have happened to me,” he said. “Failure is the greatest teacher, one of the greatest teachers that we can have in any given situation because in that failure, you have one of two paths. You either give up or you keep going.”

In Guarini’s case, he chose the latter. In fact, after independently releasing his second album in 2005, he found opportunities in television before making his Broadway debut in Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown in 2010.

Rediscovering his love for the craft, the performer went on to appear in multiple Broadway productions, including American Idiot, Romeo and Juliet and Wicked.

“I realized that there were still people celebrating me,” he said. “I realized there was still something worth celebrating in my life. And it wasn’t the vanity metrics of how many people voted for me or how many followers I would end up having or the amount of money I could make or blah, blah.”

Rather, as he put it, “It was just doing something and going back to something that I really truly loved.”

Keep reading to see where more American Idol stars are today…

The mom of River and Remy has come a long way since experiencing a moment like this on the inaugural season of American Idol in 2002. The New York resident has collected three Grammys, notched three No. 1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100, starred on NBC's The Voice as a judge and is now hosting the final season of her award-winning daytime talk show, The Kelly Clarkson Show.

The season two runner-up made two big reveals in September 2008—announcing that the birth of his son Parker (with his close friend, music producer Jaymes Foster) inspired him to come out. "I can't raise a kid and teach him how to lie, teach him to hide things," he reasoned on Good Morning America. But he hasn't totally left music in the rearview, even touring the country with season two champ Ruben Studdard in 2023 and 2024.

After winning season two of Idol, Ruben went on to score a Grammy nomination and released a handful of successful albums. Then, in 2013, the singer starred as one of the contestants on The Biggest Loser and quickly became a fan-favorite. He was eliminated twice, but took away valuable lessons from the show. And while he and Clay remain tight, he found his forever partner in wife Kristin, who welcomed their second child in 2024.

Truth is, the season three champion is grateful for every step of her journey. "We go through things, you fall, you get back up," she shared with E! News in December 2023. Said the North Carolina native, also mom to adult daughter Zion, "I want to enjoy this and know that I worked hard to get here."

She may not have won season three, but we are telling you the musician made up for it: First an Oscar for 2006's Dreamgirls, then a Grammy for her performance The Color Purple musical adaption in 2017, plus a stint as a judge on The Voice. The latest project for the mom to son David: Her own eponymous talk show.

From the moment she stepped onto the Idol stage, Carrie cemented her place in pop culture. Sure enough, not only did she win season four, but she's also gone on to become country music's reigning princess. She went on to co-host the CMA Awards for more than 10 years with fellow artist Brad Paisley. And between balancing her music career with her hosting duties, the "Jesus Take The Wheel" singer is a mom to her two sons with retired NHL center Mike Fisher.

In 2024, Carrie's return to American Idol was announced, this time as the successor to Katy Perry as one of the show's judges.

The season four runner-up is now married with three boys and a girl. Despite suffering serious health problems in 2006, the Southern rocker has released multiple hit albums since his stint on Idol.

With his big hair and even bigger voice, Constantine—who wowed with his rousing rendition of "Bohemian Rhapsody" during season four—was a perfect fit for Broadway's Rock of Ages, for which he earned a Tony nomination.The dad to daughter Malena (born 2010) went on to star in 2023's Rock & Roll Man.

We're just letting him do his thing. But, I would love for him to have a working understanding of all instruments a lot like his dad. I think he's on his way—that's for sure."

After American Idol, the season five finalist, who had a hit with the song "Wait for You," went to Angola where he worked alongside former Idol judge Kara DioGuardi to raise awareness for Malaria No More. As the youngest female winner, the season six champ set off some serious, well, sparks in 2007. Her success and good fortune has continued, with the star giving birth to her first son with Dana Isaiah in May 2018. In the years since, she made an emotional return to Idol and competed on the 31st season of Dancing With the Stars.

The season seven winner's big hit "Time of My Life" may reflect his singing success, but the title could just as easily apply to his endeavors offstage.
